evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:255: `if not finders or not precheck or STEP_DECIDE in succeeded:` — the guard does NOT require verify to have failed, only that decide did not succeed
src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:293: `# NO provider_provenance here, deliberately: verify failed by construction, so no verify-step record exists to carry.`

decide is a scripted op (`uses: plan_review_decide`, plan-review.yaml:202) that can raise a code error while verify already succeeded and recorded its outputs (which include provider_provenance)
advisory.finding: The verify-failure recovery path omits `provider_provenance` on the stated premise that 'verify failed by construction', but its guard (`if not finders or not precheck or STEP_DECIDE in succeeded: return None`) admits a run where verify SUCCEEDED but the scripted `decide` op failed. In that sub-case `succeeded[STEP_VERIFY]` holds a real runner-stamped provenance record that is silently dropped, so an honest record that IS available is not carried onto the verdict.
scenarios: Pass-2 verify agent step succeeds and stamps a provider record, then the deterministic `plan_review_decide` op raises (code error / contract failure) → recovery emits an INDETERMINATE verdict with `provider_provenance` absent despite a real provider having served the verification.
